title: Tersarge / Crab Meadow
summary: Tersarge is a seventeenth-century locality on Long Island's north shore. Later historical research connects the name with the Crab Meadow landscape east of Huntington.
address_label: Crab Meadow Wetlands and Beach, Northport, NY (general area)
map_geometry_source: Broad Crab Meadow public-land reference point supported by local historical research and modern official habitat mapping.
activity_update_summary: Removed a short introduction that repeated the listing summary.
why_this_matters: Tersarge ties a surviving Native place name to a documented claim of kinship and inheritance on the north shore. Placing it broadly at Crab Meadow makes the history visible while avoiding a false claim that the seventeenth-century allotment boundary has been precisely reconstructed.
history_content: The petition belongs to a contested history of Native kinship, colonial land claims, and the Crab Meadow landscape. The marker is placed at the modern public wetland and beach area as a broad reference point rather than a reconstructed seventeenth-century parcel.
translation_content: No secure translation for Tersarge has been established. The documentary location can be discussed more confidently than the name's linguistic meaning.
preservation_content: This draft keeps the Tersarge references available while marking it for location and citation review before publication.
whereintheworld_content: The marker is placed at Crab Meadow Wetlands and Beach, north of Northport. It represents the general historical landscape associated with Tersarge, not an exact parcel boundary.
